Between self-avoiding and $Θ$ conditions, activity dominates by introducing an emergent folding length scale, which acts as an active blob length. In this regime, we demonstrate that the ratio of thermal to active length scales provides a new scaling variable that leads to a universal master curve for active polymer collapse.

papers.title: When the core ate the atmosphere
papers.abstract: The initial volatile element inventories in a planet's atmosphere, mantle, and core are established by delivery and transport during planetary growth. Conversely, the volatile abundances of Earth's planetary reservoirs record its accretion pathway. We model here volatile transport during planet formation for two different delivery scenarios, via pebble and planetesimal accretion, to predict the volatile inventories of proto-Earth at the end of its main accretion phase. We find that the distributions of volatiles between the atmosphere, mantle, and core exhibit strong sensitivity to volatile delivery timing, metal-silicate partition coefficients, atmosphere-magma solubilities, and planet mass. In particular, the early volatile delivery expected in pebble accretion scenarios substantially enhances core sequestration of hydrogen and carbon relative to continuous delivery during incremental planetesimal accretion. With our fiducial partition coefficients, the pebble accretion model produces a 760 bar carbon-dominated atmosphere with 39 bar of hydrogen and water and a few bars of nitrogen, consistent with volatile concentration estimates for bulk silicate Earth including the atmosphere. The corresponding planetesimal accretion model produces a more massive ($\sim$$1350$ bar) atmosphere with similar composition. The core stores $\sim$$70$% of both the H and the C budget in the early-delivery scenario, but $\lesssim$$50$% in the corresponding continuous delivery scenario. Overall our results demonstrate that substantial amounts of volatiles are sequestered into rocky planet cores during planet formation and that the volatile inventory of bulk silicate Earth was likely established already during the magma ocean phase of planet formation.

papers.title: Foundations of the Scaling Law
papers.abstract: Empirical scaling laws relate loss to parameters $N$, training tokens $D$ and compute $C$. This technical note explains three mechanisms behind their exponents. Local approximation bounds function error at rate $N_e^{-γs/d}$, with effective parameters $N_e$, smoothness $s$, reuse exponent $γ$ and dimension $d$; the loss function determines the risk bound. Independent feature coverage gives $α_D=(β-1)/ζ$ from predictive-weight decay $β$ and occurrence rarity $ζ$. Separable-loss optimization determines training allocations and deployment crossovers. Nonlinear scoring can produce apparent emergent abilities, while grokking concerns delayed generalization and verification constrains test-time scaling. For regular molecular configurations, the $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ quotient gives $d_{\mathrm{int}}=d-6$ and relative approximation-exponent gain $6/d_{\mathrm{int}}$. Optimized dense-to-equivariant excess-loss ratios scale as $C^{p_{\mathrm{eq}}-p_{\mathrm{dense}}}$, where $p_j$ are compute-loss exponents and the prefactor depends on loss amplitudes and FLOP costs. Domain examples also cover visual resolution, conformational coverage and correlated-sample precision.

papers.title: Are Linguistic and Arithmetic Circuits Dissociated in LLMs?
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) exhibit both knowledge of language, rendered by, for example, grammatical judgment ability, and abilities to perform tasks through language, such as math-word problem solving. Motivated by neurolinguistic studies of their neural dissociation in human brains, in this study, we investigate the overlap of their circuits in large language models (LLMs). Specifically, we examine the overlap and causal effects between the circuits extracted for linguistic and arithmetic tasks, using controlled materials and circuit discovery methods from the mechanistic interpretability field. Our experiments with five LLMs show that circuit similarity is mostly explained by task domains (linguistic vs. arithmetic), rather than by their input and output vocabularies or by the syntactic similarities between natural-language sentences and arithmetic expressions. This finding suggests that LLMs may process linguistic and arithmetic information using largely separate neural circuits, highlighting an ability-based modular organization of circuits within these models.

papers.title: Suppression and reemergence of directional transport across the ferromagnetic transition in SrRuO$_3$
papers.abstract: SrRuO$_3$ is a canonical itinerant ferromagnet that continues to serve as a fertile platform for exploring spin-orbit coupled transport and topological responses in correlated oxide metals. Here, we investigate a (110)-oriented epitaxial SrRuO3 thin film on DyScO$_3$, where crystallographic anisotropy allows for symmetry-resolved charge transport along orthogonal in-plane directions. We uncover two principal findings. First, the resistance above the Curie temperature $T_{c,on}\approx 165$ K exhibits strong anisotropy, consistent with directionally dependent spin-fluctuation scattering. Below $T_{c,on}$, this anisotropy nearly vanishes, despite persistent structural inequivalence, due to isotropic electron-magnon and electron-electron scattering processes. Second, the application of a magnetic field reveals a striking directional contrast in the linear magnetoresistance (MR): it remains negative and saturates along [001], but changes sign and becomes positive along $[1\bar{1}0]$ below $T_0=145$ K. In contrast, the quadratic MR term is identical for both directions and peaks near $T_{\mathrm{OHE}}^*=155$ K, where the ordinary Hall coefficient crosses zero, consistent with carrier compensation under a two-band scenario. A sign change in the anomalous Hall signal at $T_{\mathrm{AHE}}^*=150$ K is consistent with a temperature-dependent redistribution of Berry-curvature contributions near the Fermi level. These results establish ferromagnetic ordering as the primary driver of the observed directional magnetotransport in SrRuO$_3$.

papers.title: Narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened multilevel atomic system
papers.abstract: We theoretically investigate narrowband nonreciprocal transmission in a Doppler-broadened five-level M-type atomic medium. After Doppler averaging, the M-type system retains a narrow near-resonant electromagnetically induced transparency window that is narrower than that of a standard three-level $Λ$ system. This spectral narrowing is associated with the decreasing separation between the two inner dressed states as atomic velocity increases. The transparency window exhibits pronounced direction-dependent transmission, with high forward transmission and strong suppression in the reverse direction. The transparency linewidth and forward-backward probe transmission can be controlled via two independent driving fields, while the central transparency frequency is kept essentially unchanged. The resulting narrowband nonreciprocity supports high forward transmission together with strong suppression in the reverse direction, which is suitable for frequency-selective optical filtering and nonreciprocal optical transmission in thermal atomic media. Our scheme with these specific features is geared towards enabling compact vapor-cell-based nonreciprocal devices for quantum network applications.

papers.title: TerraNostra-Bench: Benchmarking Spatial Downscaling and Temporal Rollout for Global 1-km Land-Use Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Uncertainty in the terrestrial carbon cycle remains a major constraint in climate projections, partly due to imperfect land surface representations in Earth system models. We propose a data-driven framework for high-resolution land-use reconstruction, treated as a semantic-segmentation task, that combines coarse-resolution scenario data and climate classification with static geophysical features to produce annual land-use maps at 1 km resolution. We introduce TerraNostra-Bench, a change-aware evaluation protocol that separates spatial downscaling from autoregressive temporal rollout and scores models on the rare land-use-change pixels rather than the dominant static background. Using it, we compare convolutional (U-Net) and transformer (Swin) backbones in autoregressive and non-autoregressive schemes against persistence, linear, and shallow convolutional baselines. The autoregressive prior is the most informative input yet accumulates error over long rollouts: autoregressive models lose 5.7-7.2 accuracy points over 13 years, against 2.2-2.8 for non-autoregressive models. This trade-off is governed by the autoregressive choice rather than the backbone. It can be tuned by an inference-time prior-trust threshold that requires no retraining and by the training-time weighting of reconstruction and change objectives; the two levers trace complementary frontiers, with calibration recovering up to 10 accuracy points while keeping change sensitivity above the persistence floor. Extrapolating beyond the training window, backward to 1955-1959 and forward to 2015-2019 under scenario forcing, the models retain most of their in-window skill and show the same trade-off, indicating it is intrinsic to the design. This work provides the methodological foundation and evaluation surface for a forthcoming temporally continuous land-use product.

papers.title: Multi-View Latent Action Pretraining for Cross-Embodiment Robot Learning from Videos
papers.abstract: Action-free videos are an appealing substitute for costly teleoperated data. Latent action models (LAMs) turn videos into a supervision signal by inferring abstract actions between frames. Existing LAMs observe a single camera view, which resolves 6D robot actions only ambiguously missing out-of-plane movements and potential occlusions. We propose a LAM that ingests synchronized multi-camera views using cross-attention to resolve depth and occlusions before compressing them into latent actions. The latent actions are fed into a policy in which a latent expert and an action expert are coupled by sequential flow matching around a frozen VLM backbone. We further evaluate in strict cross-embodiment settings where task-specific demonstrations come from other embodiments. We show that dual-view LAM pretraining improves the decodability of ground-truth 6D actions by 17% compared to single-view, while scaling single-view data by two orders of magnitude is not sufficient to fully recover out-of-plane motions. The downstream policy improves success rate by +13.5% compared to +6.2% for single-view LAM. A single cross-embodiment is sufficient for skill transfer, and adding a second viewpoint outperforms adding up to four further embodiments. The results transfer to hardware where demonstrations come from a human hand improving success rate by +20% over action-only policies in 850 rollouts. We show that video and robot data are complementary, and that benefits of learning from video are task-dependent. Website: https://learnsyslab.github.io/multiview_latent_action_pretraining/

papers.title: Metrization of the Fell Topology and the Wijsman Topology for the Box Metric on Closed Downward Families
papers.abstract: We study nonempty Box-closed families of metric measure spaces that are downward under the Lipschitz order. If a space is below a member in this order, it also belongs to the family. Such families need not be pyramids, because directedness is an additional condition. We define a metric on these families by taking the supremum, over all finite metric measure spaces, of the normalized absolute difference between the infimal Box distances from each finite space to the two families. We divide each difference by the sum of the support cardinality and diameter of the finite test space. The topology induced by this metric agrees on the full domain with the relative Fell topology and with the restriction of the Wijsman topology for the Box metric. On the subspace of pyramids, it induces the weak topology and makes the natural inclusion into the hyperspace of nonempty closed subsets a topological embedding for either hyperspace topology. Pyramids associated with metric measure spaces are dense in the pyramid space, which is the completion of metric measure spaces under the metric pulled back along the map that sends each space to its associated pyramid.

papers.title: Absolute winning properties of exceptional sets for rational maps
papers.abstract: We study Schmidt's game on the Julia set $J(f)$ of weak hyperbolic rational maps $f:\CC\to\CC$. For each $y\in J(f)$, let $E(f,y)$ be the set of points in $J(f)$ whose forward orbits stay a positive distance from $y$. We prove that $E(f,y)$ is absolute winning on $J(f)$ for each $y \in J(f)$. To do this, we first prove the absolute winning property for the exceptional set associated to the critical points by a potential game argument, and then use uniform expansion to obtain the result for each target point $y$.

papers.title: Toward Agentic AI for the 6G Physical Layer: From Algorithm Discovery to Verified Baseband Silicon
papers.abstract: 6G will be designed faster than it can be built: AI-driven search already proposes physical-layer algorithms at machine speed, while carrying a single one onto embedded baseband silicon remains specialist work. That silicon imposes hard memory and numeric limits, but also exposes cost structures a GPU lacks, and a design flow that never runs on the target sees neither. We present an agentic workflow in which an LLM coding agent implements algorithms on a commercial baseband SoC, optimizes them down to agent-written vector assembly, and validates them on silicon. The agent is guided by a knowledge base of measured platform facts, checked at every step against evaluators it is instructed never to edit, and metered per phase. We showcase the workflow on an AI-discovered orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) detector portfolio on the open 6G4All platform. It yields twelve kernels that run cycle-exactly on silicon, their optimized versions at 18k-405k cycles (30-660 $μ$s) per frame. It also yields a new detector shaped by the chip's measured costs that needs 13.9% fewer cycles than the port of the discovered detector while matching its error rate, with a measured edge our evaluation cannot statistically resolve, a structure that a hardware-blind search objective had no reason to find. What is not specific to OTFS is the workflow: an LLM agent exploring an implementation space under real hardware limits, with the cost of every choice measured rather than assumed.

papers.title: Accelerating real-time hybrid-functional calculations with learned ACE and symmetry-based FFT reuse
papers.abstract: Real-time hybrid-functional calculations require repeated reconstruction of nonlocal exchange, whose cost grows rapidly with Brillouin-zone sampling. We develop two methods to improve the efficiency of time evolution and spatial processing. The first learns the time evolution of adaptively compressed exchange (ACE) factors and predicts their updates, reducing the frequency of explicit reconstruction. The second uses crystal symmetry to reuse exchange fast Fourier transforms (FFTs) among equivalent real-space points. This symmetry-based FFT reuse (SBFR) reduces the number of FFTs while retaining the full $\bm k$-point sum. The methods can be used with a variety of hybrid functionals, and we use HSE06 in this work. Relative to an ACE reference using full-row mesh FFTs, learned prediction provides more than fivefold acceleration, SBFR more than fourteenfold, and their combination more than sixty-threefold. The combined method shows efficient parallel scaling. After learning, propagation takes less than 0.5 s per step. The reduced computational cost allows us to study nonlinear and nonequilibrium electron dynamics with hybrid functionals and to examine the role of excitonic effects in semiconductors and insulators.

papers.title: ProtoEEG: Structured Prototype Alignment for EEG Visual Decoding
papers.abstract: EEG visual decoding remains difficult because scalp recordings are noisy, spatially coarse, and variable across trials and subjects. Most systems align each trial with a dense image embedding, although that embedding mixes semantic content with instance-specific texture, pose, and background. This target can demand details absent from EEG and provides no explicit account of the visual factors supporting a prediction. We propose \textbf{ProtoEEG}, a prototype-mediated framework that reformulates EEG--image alignment as soft composition over a shared learnable visual codebook. A trainable EEG encoder and a frozen visual teacher produce assignment distributions over the same $K=64$ prototypes. Their weighted reconstructions form a structured representation for retrieval and image generation. Prototype contrast supplies the main cross-modal training signal, distribution alignment coordinates codebook use across modalities, an instance anchor preserves fine-grained discrimination, and diversity regularization prevents redundant prototypes. The shared assignment profile also makes the learned bottleneck directly testable through prototype retention, random selection, and identity shuffling. Across five seeds, ProtoEEG reaches 64.0\% Top-1 and 91.5\% Top-5 on THINGS-EEG2 200-way retrieval. After retraining on EEG-ImageNet, it obtains 44.8\% Top-1 and 73.8\% Top-5 in 80-way retrieval. ProtoEEG also ranks first on all seven reconstruction metrics. Removing prototype contrast lowers Top-1 by 56.9 percentage points, while shuffling prototype identities reduces it to 0.5\%. Prototype analyses further show distributed assignments and broad codebook use rather than one-prototype routing. These results support structured alignment targets as a practical alternative to increasing encoder or teacher capacity alone.

papers.title: New Directions in Irrationality
papers.abstract: Since Apéry's proof of the irrationality of $ζ(3)$, decades of work have explored integrals, hypergeometric identities, and recurrences with exceptional arithmetic properties, to discover the strongest quantitative bounds on irrationality measures for zeta values and related constants. Yet, most findings have relied on specially tailored families of such constructions, making their systematic extension difficult. Here we show how these constructions can be connected and generalized into a common multidimensional structure based on conservative matrix fields (CMFs), enabling a systematic discovery of new irrationality proofs and quantitative bounds for irrationality exponents. CMFs are finite-dimensional cocycles of compatible rational matrix shifts, and are shown to capture all the classical constructions developed since Apéry as one-dimensional trajectories. The initial point encodes the mathematical constants; varying the trajectory within a suitable convergence region produces different approximation schemes for the same constants. We use this structure to improve the irrationality measures of famous constants, yielding for example $μ(ζ(2))<4.62675$ and $μ(ζ(3))<5.4197$, and proving that $1,ζ(3),ζ(4)$ are linearly independent over $\mathbb{Q}$, yielding $μ(Aζ(3)+Bζ(4))<66.3$ for every $(A,B)\in\mathbb{Q}^2\setminus\{(0,0)\}$. The same approach demonstrated over other CMFs provides irrationality proving trajectories for infinitely more mathematical constants. We further construct higher-rank CMFs with explicit initial states for $1,ζ(2),ζ(3),\ldots,ζ(d+1)$, and identify the arithmetic conditions needed to obtain further, higher-order independence results.

papers.title: Decoupled Representation Learning for Face Presentation Attack Detection under Smart Glass Capture
papers.abstract: Face presentation attack detection is typically studied under fixed camera or handheld acquisition, whereas smart glass capture introduces a more challenging setting with ego motion, changing viewpoint, background clutter, distance variation, and less controlled illumination. To address this challenge, we present \emph{SmaGla-FPAD}, a smart glass based face presentation attack database acquired using Ray-Ban Meta Wayfarer Smart Glasses across indoor, outdoor, and in-car settings. The database contains 297,000 sample images with both bona fide and silicone mask based attacks. We further propose \emph{DeCoupPAD-FAS++}, a decoupled representation learning framework that separates spoof related evidence from nuisance sensitive capture variation through complementary attack and style branches, pseudo-domain supervision, adversarial suppression, and prompt guided semantic alignment. Experiments on SmaGla-FPAD show that the proposed method achieves the best balance between attack rejection and bona fide acceptance in both in domain and cross scenario evaluation. Ablation results further confirm the contribution of disentanglement, pseudo-domain supervision, and prompt based regularisation under smart glass capture.

papers.title: Looks Fine to Me: Understanding Oversight in Agentic Interactions
papers.abstract: Agentic AI systems are deployed to execute complex tasks across domains such as writing, coding, and data analysis. As execution is offloaded to AI agents, the human role shifts toward oversight. Effective oversight requires recognizing when closer scrutiny is needed, even though flawed outputs may appear convincing. Our formative study (N=12) revealed that users accepted plausible outputs without thorough evaluation, and only recognized these lapses in retrospect. To examine this systematically, we conducted a controlled within-subject study (N=36) in which participants completed programming tasks with an agent that produced correct outputs, silent defects, or visible failures. Combining task outcomes, interaction logs, gaze, physiological signals, and self-reports, we examined perceived, behavioral, and effective oversight. Participants were often highly confident while missing silent defects: they performed generic checks, failed to generate diagnostic evidence, or even misinterpreted defect evidence. We discuss how studying oversight across multiple dimensions can support future work on timely, task-calibrated re-engagement.

papers.title: Collective Hall quantization in 3D Chern vector systems
papers.abstract: Understanding the three-dimensional (3D) quantum Hall effect, characterized by a Chern vector rather than a single Chern number, has been a central pursuit in topological physics. While quantized Hall transport is established for the special case with one nonzero Chern component, recent realizations of more general Chern-vector states raise a fundamental question: how does such topology protect quantized transport? Here, we predict a distinct 3D quantized Hall effect protected by $\mathbf{C}=(0,m,n)$. For samples with dimensions $L_y$ and $L_z$, global topology enforces collective quantization of $mL_y+nL_z$, despite the fragility of individual edge modes to disorder. This reveals a novel transport regime in which robust quantization emerges as a holistic property of a unified chiral network,rather than of its constituent modes. Crucially, this collective response manifests as a quantized Hall conductance $G_{xy}=\pm(mL_y+nL_z)e^2/h$, with a distinctive dependence on both Chern-vector components and sample dimensions. We propose candidate materials to facilitate experimental observation.

papers.title: The strong type endpoint estimate for the local spherical maximal function
papers.abstract: Let $p_d=(d^2+1)/(d(d-1))$ and $q_d=(d^2+1)/(d-1)$. We prove that the local spherical maximal operator $\sup_{1\leq t\leq 2}|f*dσ_t|$ is bounded from $L^{p_d}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ to $L^{q_d}(\mathbb{R}^d)$ for every $d\geq 2$. Previously only the restricted weak type estimate was known at this endpoint. Together with known results, this completes the characterization of the strong type $L^p\to L^q$ bounds for the local spherical maximal operator. We also prove the maximal estimate \[ \Big\|\sup_{t\in\mathbb{R}}|e^{it\sqrt{-Δ}}f|\Big\|_{L^{2(d+1)/(d-1)}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \lesssim\|f\|_{\dot H^{d/(d+1)}(\mathbb{R}^d)} \] for the wave equation at the critical exponent. Both results are obtained by exploiting the gain in bilinear estimates that comes from the interaction between high and low frequencies.

papers.title: Weyl Bounds for $\operatorname{GL}_2\times \operatorname{GL}_2$ Rankin--Selberg $L$-functions via Short Spectral Moments
papers.abstract: Let $f$ and $g$ be Hecke--Maass cusp forms of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$, with spectral parameters $t_f$ and $t_g$, respectively. Let $T$ be a large parameter and put $L = |T-t_g|.$ We prove the Lindelöf-on-average estimate \[ \sum_{ |t_f-T|\leq H} \left|L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right)\right|^2 \ll_{\varepsilon} T^{1+\varepsilon}H, \] uniformly in the range \[ T^{1/3+\varepsilon}\ll H,\qquad HT^\varepsilon\ll L\leq T. \] As an immediate consequence, in the generic range when both $|t_g|$ and $L$ are of size $T$, we obtain the Weyl bound \[ L\!\left(\frac12,f\otimes g\right) \ll_\varepsilon C(f\times g)^{1/6+\varepsilon}. \]

papers.title: Certified Adaptive List Decoding for Error-Correcting Codes
papers.abstract: Maximum-likelihood (ML) decoding of linear block codes is NP-hard, so neural decoders are evaluated by how closely they approach it. We observe that proving a candidate optimal can be far easier than finding it, and build a decoder that does both. We cast decoding as a search over an absorbing-state discrete diffusion model, whose sequential commitment of coordinates turns generation into a tree, and run a probability beam search over it. A dual bound from a linear-programming relaxation and a distance-based test, both derived from the code, then certify per frame that the current candidate is the global ML solution; because both are theorems, certified frames incur no accuracy-computation trade-off. Across $15$ codes and five operating points we certify up to $99.9\%$ of frames, the two tests dividing the space as their derivations predict, one strong for sparse parity-check matrices and the other for codes with a large minimum distance. Certification also behaves as a per-frame reliability signal, with $96.7$-$100\%$ of all frame errors falling on uncertified frames. Against an exact ML reference at $5$ dB the decoder is within one standard deviation on three of the four codes where the reference is uncensored, and against four neural baselines it attains the best bit-error rate in $71$ of $75$ cells.

papers.title: Probing the Optical/UV Continuum Variability of Active Galactic Nuclei with the Damped Random Walk Model
papers.abstract: Optical/UV continuum variability over baselines of up to 20 yr is investigated using the damped random walk (DRW) model for 1214 active galactic nuclei (AGNs) compiled from Y. Shen et al. and C. J. Burke et al. Among these, 115 AGNs with reliable DRW fitting and unbiased DRW parameters (timescale $τ_{2500}$ and amplitude $σ_{2500}$ at the rest-frame 2500~Å) are used to examine the relations between the variability and the accretion properties. We found a significant correlation of $τ_{2500}$ with black hole mass ($M_{\rm BH}$) and dimensionless accretion rate ($\dot{\mathscr{M}}$) of the form $τ_{2500} \propto M_{\rm BH}^{0.50\pm0.07} \dot{\mathscr{M}}^{0.27\pm0.04}$, while the dependence on the continuum luminosity at 5100~Å and redshift becomes insignificant after controlling for $M_{\rm BH}$. $τ_{2500}$ also correlate with the mass accretion rate ($\dot{M}$) as $τ_{2500} \propto \dot{M}^{0.41\pm0.04}$, which is consistent with the thermal timescale expected from the standard thin-disk model within $3σ$ uncertainties; while the average value is consistent with the expectations of the model, the scatter in the relation can be due to differences in the viscosity parameter ($α$) or in disk temperature profiles. Assuming that \tauuv\ corresponds to the accretion disk thermal timescale, the disk-emitting radius at rest-frame 2500~Å ($R_{2500}$) is found to correlate with $M_{\rm BH}$ as $R_{2500} \propto M_{\rm BH}^{0.53\pm0.05}$. Using the microlensing-based $R_{2500}-M_{\rm BH}$ relation of C. W. Morgan et al., $α$ is statistically estimated to be $0.04\pm0.01$.

papers.title: What Shapes the Ultraviolet Spectra of Type Ia Supernovae?
papers.abstract: Ultraviolet (UV) observations of Type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) exhibit significant diversity, but their physical origin remains poorly understood. We investigate UV spectra of SNe Ia observed with the Swift UltraViolet and Optical Telescope. Our expanded pre-maximum sample probes dependencies on decline rate, ejecta properties, and host environment. We recover the correlation between UV flux and decline rate near maximum in the near-UV (NUV), and find correlations at pre-maximum phases in both the NUV and mid-UV (MUV). This trend is strongly wavelength dependent, with slow decliners showing higher NUV but lower MUV flux than fast decliners. Synthetic TARDIS spectra varying the 56Ni abundance show that enhanced 56Ni suppresses the MUV while increasing the NUV, broadly reproducing the trend. We find no significant correlation between UV flux and ejecta velocity, while Si II 6355 pEW shows trends similar to those with decline rate. We also find no significant correlations with host-galaxy properties, although host environment may contribute to the remaining UV diversity among SNe with similar decline rates. Early-excess SNe show enhanced flux mainly in the NUV rather than a broad UV excess, suggesting that strong circumstellar interaction is not necessarily required to explain the observed excess emission. Peculiar subclasses show distinct UV properties, with brighter and hotter subclasses showing higher UV flux, although the current sample is small and does not cover all SN Ia subtypes. Our results suggest that the UV diversity of SNe Ia is shaped by multiple mechanisms that contribute differently across the UV wavelength range.

papers.title: Atomic identification via the Prandtl-Tomlinson stick-slip mechanism
papers.abstract: Distinguishing atomic species is an ongoing challenge in the field of scanning probe microscopy. Typically, atomic force microscopy makes use of electrostatic interactions to perform atomic identification. Here we perform lateral force microscopy (LFM) measurements with a CO terminated tip of a partially oxidized Cu(110) surface and show clear differences between the metal and oxygen sites over a large z-range. This allows for atomic identification on a typical metal oxide. Density functional theory based calculations show that the tip-sample interaction is dominated by short-ranged orbital interactions and that the electrostatic contribution is negligible. At small tip-sample distances, LFM can probe the Prandtl-Tomlinson stick-slip mechanism on the single-atom scale. It is visible as a striking asymmetry in the forward and backward scan directions, experimentally revealing this fundamental model for nanotribology on the single-atom scale.

papers.title: Non-null ruled surfaces and pseudo hyper-dual tangent sphere bundles
papers.abstract: In this paper, the tangent bundles of hyper-dual pseudo spheres are defined. Then, a new family of non-null ruled surfaces associated with hyper-dual Lorentzian curves is defined via the E.Study hyper-map in Minkowski space and the definitions of the tangent bundles of hyper-dual pseudo spheres. Within this framework, the resulting non-null ruled surfaces are classified. Necessary and sufficient conditions for developability are obtained with their geometric interpretations in terms of hyper-dual Lorentzian curves and arc-length parameters. Moreover, explicit examples are presented to verify the theoretical results.

papers.title: Phonon Dispersion Relation in Weakly Coupled Bose Gas Beyond Bogoliubov Approximation
papers.abstract: We study the quasiparticle dispersion relation for a homogeneous Bose gas in a large cubic box with periodic boundary conditions at zero temperature. Inspired by the Bogoliubov method, we rearrange the usual Bose gas Hamiltonian in a form adapted to perturbation theory in the weak-coupling regime, both in the canonical and grand-canonical setting. We compute the first non-trivial corrections to the dispersion relation in both settings. We show that for small momenta they are linear in the absolute value of the momentum. Thus, in this approximation phonons have a well-defined velocity, which we compute.

papers.title: A Transport-Information Framework for Continuous-Fiber-Aligned Coarse-Graining Representation Sets
papers.abstract: Consider representation sets of interest whose elements are associated with continuous realizations related to them through coarse-graining (CG). CG can be regarded as an operation that reduces a representation by discarding information that is not retained in its output. However, a systematic description of the information structure associated with CG in general remains to be established. Here, we propose a transport-information framework for continuous-fiber-aligned representation sets, in which each representation is associated with a continuous realization through a fiber structure, with CG defining the projection onto the representation. Within this framework, CG is described through a local-map operation that transports continuous probability mass onto representative points. The resulting transport cost is expressed as the contraction of the second-moment structure of the underlying continuous representation with the transport metric. Building on the previously proposed framework of unavoidable canonical nonlinearity (UCN), this construction provides a non-arbitrary information-theoretic interpretation of the CG-associated transport cost in terms of information indistinguishability, quantified by an expected second-order structure on statistical manifold associated with the CG geometry. We also show that the proposed framework can also be naturally extended to the CG of the discrete measures themselves. The present framework provides a basis for describing information costs associated with individual CG operations and for comparing representation sets while accounting for their underlying continuous realizations.

papers.title: SliMOO: Interpretable Multi-Objective Evolutionary Search for LLM Depth Pruning
papers.abstract: As large language models (LLMs) grow more powerful, their scale makes them costly to serve. Depth pruning offers a practical route to efficiency by directly reducing memory and latency without hardware-specific support. However, we observe that transformer layers exhibit markedly different task-dependent layer contributions, whereas existing depth-pruning methods ignore this heterogeneity and thus tend to optimize for a narrow domain or benchmark rather than preserve broad capability. This suggests that LLM depth pruning should be formulated as a multi-objective optimization problem rather than a single-score ranking problem. We propose SliMOO, an interpretable multi-objective evolutionary search framework for LLM depth pruning. SliMOO first uses single-layer removal probing to construct a task-layer importance map, which provides an interpretable view of task-shared and task-specific layers and serves as a search prior. It then performs a Pareto-aware evolutionary search for pruning masks, where candidates are generated under the guidance of the task-layer prior, scored by their deviation from the dense model on each task, and retained through NSGA-II environmental selection. Across the Llama-3.1 and Qwen3 model families, SliMOO consistently achieves stronger multi-task trade-offs than rule-based, greedy, and scalarized baselines. For example, on Llama-3.1-70B at 25% sparsity, it improves the math-domain average from 24.33% to 34.40% and the code-domain average from 35.03% to 39.14%. Code will be made available at https://github.com/AMD-AGI/SliMOO.

papers.title: LatBridge: Efficient and Stable Model Replacement in Latent-Communication Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Multi-agent systems rely on communication to complete tasks, and latent communication passes continuous representations to reduce text generation and re-encoding. However, multi-agent systems must reconfigure agent models, whereas existing latent-communication methods are built for fixed model combinations, so their interfaces may fail after replacement. Our pilot study confirms this interface failure and identifies the requirement for interface reuse after model replacement. We present LatBridge, which connects agent models through a shared Bridge and separate interfaces under a shared latent-communication protocol. After agent model replacement, LatBridge reuses unchanged interfaces, selects matching low-rank interfaces, and combines them through the Bridge, training only missing ones with all models frozen. The Bridge processes source representations in the basic mode and constructs target input without autoregressive generation in the accelerated mode. Experiments support effective communication after model replacement, with mean basic-mode accuracies of 14.8% on MATH and 27.3% on ALFWorld next-action prediction across eight small-model configurations. Analyses examine the factors supporting task accuracy and communication efficiency.

papers.title: The Dimension Landscape of Bivariate $C^2$ Splines
papers.abstract: Schumaker's lower bound incorporates local geometric corrections and provides insight into the dimensions of bivariate spline spaces. Building on this bound, we study bivariate $C^2$ spline dimensions from three perspectives: universal attainment, generic attainment, and geometric jumps. We prove universal attainment in degree seven for every legal realization of every triangulation. We prove generic attainment in degrees five and six for every fixed combinatorial triangulation and give explicit polynomial conditions certifying generic failure on fixed triangulations in degrees three and four. For geometric jumps with matching local direction types at corresponding interior vertices, we prove nonexistence in degree seven and construct examples in degrees three and five. In degree six, universal attainment and the existence of such geometric jumps remain open questions.

papers.title: ProVe: Proposer-Verifier Decoding
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates autoregressive (AR) language models by letting a small model draft tokens serially and a large model verify them in parallel. We reverse these roles. Starting from a standard AR checkpoint, we fine-tune the large model into a proposer that predicts a block of future tokens in a single forward pass, then use one additional forward pass to verify the proposed block. This gives ProVe, Proposer-Verifier decoding. The verifier can be a smaller AR model or the proposer itself; the latter gives ProVe-lossless, which reproduces the proposer's greedy AR decoding. Block proposals already provide substantial room for acceleration: with a block size of 16, the proposed block has an average AR-matching prefix of 6.6 tokens on GSM8K. Across six benchmarks with a 32B proposer, ProVe-lossless reaches 2.5x average AR throughput without training a separate draft head. With a small 3B verifier, ProVe reaches 2.7x average throughput at 2.6 accuracy points below AR on the six-task average, providing a controllable tradeoff between speed and accuracy.

papers.title: RAG-NIMBF: A Non-Invasive, Modular Benchmarking Framework for Automated RAG Configuration Analysis
papers.abstract: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) has become the dominant paradigm for grounding the outputs of large language models (LLM) in external knowledge. However, practitioners are faced with a vast configuration space comprising chunking, embedding, retrieval, reranking, prompting and generation models, and there is limited guidance on how these components interact. We present RAG-NIMBF, a modular benchmarking framework that attaches to existing RAG pipelines as a non-invasive evaluation layer. It evaluates the configuration space through controlled ablation with end-to-end experiment tracking. The evaluation combines LLM-based answer quality scores, retrieval correctness measures, and runtime indicators. This study validates the framework across multiple generation models on the SQuAD dataset. This process reveals non-obvious interactions and demonstrates how the experiments are tracked. The findings indicate that the retrieval balance of relevance and diversity substantially enhances the relevance and coverage of retrieved context in comparison to a conventional similarity search, with MMR raising nDCG@5 by +4 to +11 percentage points across the swept models. More detailed prompt instructions meaningfully increase how faithfully generated answers stick to the retrieved evidence, especially for capable and reasoning models (+10 to +13pp on Qwen3.6-27B, GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3.5-think, but negligible on the 20B generator). Overall, RAG-NIMBF transforms the configuration space of RAG into reproducible, comparable experiments. By attaching to existing production pipelines in a non-invasive way, it enables practitioners to systematically evaluate and improve deployed systems without disrupting existing workflows. This replaces ad hoc choices with evidence-based decisions.

papers.title: Privacy-preserving inference on hosted models: a learned input-embedding transform for frozen Qwen3.8-27B
papers.abstract: Every prompt sent to a hosted language model is readable by whoever runs it. We study whether the prompt can remain on the client while the host receives transformed vectors that stand in for it. A language model converts text to vectors exactly once, with a public lookup table; we perform that step locally and pass the vectors through a small trained network (55.6M parameters) before they leave the perimeter. The host runs a frozen 27B model (Qwen3.8-27B) on the transformed vectors and never receives text or token ids. We train the transform against the frozen model as a fixed judge, combining a forward-KL utility term with an auxiliary term that pushes each vector away from its original direction. On 1,490 MMLU questions held out from training, the transform costs 1.5 points of accuracy (80.7% vs. 82.3%), breaking 68 of the 1,226 questions the unmodified model answers correctly (5.5%), while 30.1% of content tokens no longer decode to their original token under a nearest-neighbour lookup.

papers.title: Strichartz Estimates and Scattering for the Massless Reduced Dirac-Fock Equation
papers.abstract: In this paper, we establish Strichartz estimates for the reduced Dirac-Fock equation for 3D massless spinors, linearized around non-localized equilibria. Our analysis covers both the random field and the density matrix frameworks. As an application, we deduce scattering for the corresponding nonlinear problem with a high-frequency cut-off.

papers.title: Ehrhart positivity of smooth polytopes with few facets
papers.abstract: For each dimension $d$, we determine the minimum number of facets of a smooth $d$-dimensional lattice polytope whose Ehrhart polynomial has at least one negative coefficient. This minimum is six in dimension $d=3$, seven in dimension $d=4$, and $d+2$ in every dimension $d\ge 5$. The lower bounds follow from the classification of smooth lattice polytopes with at most $d+2$ facets, together with explicit formulas for Ehrhart polynomials in dimensions at most $4$. We also prove that a lattice polytope of dimension at least $3$ with a smooth vertex cannot be $2$-integral with respect to any ordered lattice basis.

papers.title: SMART: Semantic Segment Mapping and Assessment of Recognition Transcripts with Contextual Rubrics
papers.abstract: Word error rate (WER) assigns equal cost to lexical edits despite their different semantic consequences, while overall semantic scores cannot identify which individual errors alter the intended meaning. We formulate ASR semantic evaluation as context-aware, segment-level consequence assessment and propose Semantic Segment Mapping and Assessment of Recognition Transcripts with Contextual Rubrics (SMART), a framework for traceable semantic evaluation and targeted ASR correction. SMART maps reference-hypothesis discrepancies into coherent segments and applies a structured contextual rubric to assign explicit consequence labels. These labels support Semantic Impact Error Rate (SIER), which quantifies consequential errors at utterance, chunk, and lexical levels. Against majority-vote human labels, SMART achieves 0.843 F1 versus 0.745 for direct LLM judgment. Evaluation across multiple LLMs further demonstrates that SMART is relatively insensitive to the choice of evaluation model, while MER and SIER reveal different aspects of ASR quality. A separate target-reference-free rubric guides correction using the target hypothesis and surrounding ASR hypotheses, outperforming a matched w/o Rubric baseline on both datasets, with further absolute reductions of 0.85-0.98 percentage points in MER and 1.18-1.65 percentage points in SIER_lex.

papers.title: Emergent non-reciprocal pair interactions in catalytically propelled active polyhedra
papers.abstract: Particle shape plays a fundamental role in the dynamics and pair interactions of active particles. Yet, experimental measurements of anisotropic active particles are largely lacking. Here, we introduce an experimental system that allows us to observe and measure the effective pair interactions of self-propelled active colloidal polyhedra. We realize such a system by 3D micro-printing quasi- 2D polyhedral colloids with edge number N= 3,4,5,6 and infinity and induce propulsion by partially coating them with an iridium catalytic cap and dispersing them in hydrazine. Despite their different geometries, all shapes exhibit similar single-particle positional dynamics. Stochastic Force Inference reveals predominantly radial, non-reciprocal pair interactions with similar attractive and repulsive regimes for all particle shapes at center-to center distances of about two particle diameters. A minimal plausible phoretic active-Brownian-particle model with a disc shape reproduces the experimentally observed behavior and identifies the physical origins: concentration-dependent slowing down sets their dominant angular symmetry, while the spatial geometry of the chemical coupling and phoretic attraction recover their relative magnitudes and angular dependence. We find that the shape anisotropy present in experiments only modulates the magnitudes and angular dependence of these interactions, and that these variations become more pronounced the stronger the anisotropy. Our results demonstrate the interplay of chemically mediated interactions and particle geometry-induced effects at intermediate interaction distances.

papers.title: COMPASS: Routing via Capability-Oriented Model Profiling with Adaptive Search, Selection, and Tool Use
papers.abstract: LLM routing aims to select a capable model at low cost, but specialized routers can require updates as models and tasks change. We propose COMPASS, an agentic router in which an LLM follows a routing recipe, gathers performance and cost evidence through tools, and optionally inspects candidate answers before selecting a model. Our evaluations on LLMRouterBench and DeepSWE show that agentic routing can improve accuracy and lower model-call cost relative to specialized and trained routing baselines, without routing-specific training. On LLMRouterBench, COMPASS reaches 69.85% accuracy at \$139.57, compared with RLCascadeRouter's 69.14% at \$180.22. On DeepSWE under fixed five-fold cross-validation, it reaches 78.1% at \$215, compared with 74.1% at \$500 for the best single model. COMPASS also supports routing across benchmarks and adapts to an expanded model pool by reading new evaluation records, without changing the router's weights or prompt.

papers.title: Luther-Emery liquid in one-dimensional attractive Fermi gas
papers.abstract: One-dimensional (1D) interacting Fermi gases underpin a rich variety of quantum liquids, ranging from the Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid and the Fulde-Ferrell-Larkin-Ovchinnikov paired state to the Luther-Emery liquid (LEL). Notably, the LEL-characterized by gapless excitations in charge or spin degree of freedom and gapped excitations in the other-has long been theoretically predicted but has eluded definitive experimental observation to date. By exactly solving the attractive Yang-Gaudin model via the Bethe ansatz, we fully determine the low-energy excitation spectra for both spin and charge channels. For fully paired fermions, the spectrum features gapped spin excitation coexisting with gapless charge excitation. We further employ bosonization to derive analytical expressions for the dynamical structure factor (DSF) of the gapped spin excitation, which is a long-standing challenge in this study. In the trapped gas, we find that the spin Bragg spectroscopy peak occurs at a much higher frequency than the charge-mode peak, where the splitting frequency between these two peaks scales approximately linearly with the interaction strength. Crucially, the spin gap manifests as a sharp threshold in the spin DSF, below which spectral weight is completely absent, proving a direct and unambiguous spectroscopic fingerprint of the LEL. Our work establishes quasi-1D trapped attractive Fermi gases as a pristine experimental platform for the long-sought direct observation of the LEL.

papers.title: Thermodynamic Supercritical Scaling Law for the charged Gauss-Bonnet AdS Black Hole
papers.abstract: The phase structure of the charged Gauss-Bonnet AdS black holes varies with the spacetime dimension. Within an appropriate parameter range, only the six-dimensional case admits two physical critical points and it is an ideal model for investigating supercritical thermodynamics in black hole systems with multiple critical points. In this study, we investigate the supercritical thermodynamic properties of this model in the extended phase space and construct the supercritical phase diagrams associated with the two critical points. The thermodynamic supercritical scaling analysis for the supercritical crossover lines in the vicinity of both critical points is completed, demonstrating universality. The corresponding coefficients for the external field scaling and the order parameter scaling are obtained, and their physical significance is discussed.

papers.title: Early-stage local melting during solid-state sintering of a Cu-Ni-Ti-Zr-Hf alloy: A combined thermodynamic and kinetic analysis
papers.abstract: Complex concentrated alloys (CCAs) combining elements from 3d transition and refractory groups, specifically Cu-Ni-Ti-Zr-Hf-based shape memory systems, exhibit excellent functional properties but present significant manufacturing challenges via powder metallurgy. In this study, a non-equimolar Cu15Ni35Ti25Zr12.5Hf12.5 (at. %) alloy was successfully produced by induction melting, followed by atomization and subsequent consolidation via Spark Plasma Sintering (SPS) at temperatures ranging from 850 to 1100 °C. Although equilibrium calculations using the current TCHEA7 database predict solid-state stability of the nominal composition up to slightly below 1100 °C, localized melting unexpectedly occurred during SPS already at 1000 °C and at 1100 °C. By combining retrospective Scheil-Gulliver solidification simulations with 2D local equilibrium heat maps, we demonstrate that this early-stage melting is not driven by macroscopic thermal gradients, but by microsegregation inherited from atomization. During solid-state heating, thermally activated short-range diffusion, accelerated by high defect densities at particle interfaces, partitions Ti towards the interparticle network, leaving Cu-enriched regions (up to ~41 at. %) within the particle interiors. Owing to the strongly negative mixing enthalpy of Cu with Hf (-19.2 kJ/mol for $ΔH_{mix}^{l-l}$) and, to a lesser extent, with Ti, the local solidus of these Cu-rich regions is dramatically depressed. Upon heating to 1100 °C, these regions cross their local solidus and form a liquid phase, whose solidification produces the Cu-Hf co-segregation. This framework accounts for localized melting phenomena in rapidly solidified CCA powders containing low-melting constituents with strong negative mixing enthalpies.

papers.title: MIMOS-Tools: An Integrated Toolchain for Model-Based Design of Embedded Systems
papers.abstract: Despite decades of progress in model-based methods and tools for embedded real-time systems, there is still no integrated environment that supports the entire development lifecycle. This paper presents MIMOS-Tools, a comprehensive toolchain spanning the key phases of development, including modeling, simulation, formal verification, real-time scheduling, schedulability and end-to-end latency analysis, and code generation for heterogeneous multicore platforms. All phases are grounded in a single, coherent, and deterministic model of computation, the MIMOS model, for which we present a formal operational semantics and establish both functional and timing determinism. This semantic foundation ensures that properties verified at the model level are preserved throughout the development process and in the generated implementation. A distinguishing feature of MIMOS-Tools is its support for not only deterministic but also modular, compositional design. Unlike synchronous design environments such as SCADE and Simulink, which rely on a global base clock and offline static scheduling, MIMOS-Tools supports time-triggered asynchronous communication together with flexible real-time scheduling of computation. This removes the tight global coupling of the synchronous paradigm: components can be added, modified, or updated without recomputing a system-wide schedule, enabling scalable and incremental design and dynamic updates throughout the system lifecycle. However, MIMOS-Tools also supports Simulink models when the deadlines of tasks are set to zero to emulate the zero-time semantics of synchronous design. The toolchain is available at uu-mimos.github.io.

papers.title: Robust and Sparse Personalized Federated Learning via Gamma-Divergence
papers.abstract: To address the challenges of statistical heterogeneity across clients and within-client data contamination in federated learning, we propose a robust and sparse personalized federated learning method based on the gamma-divergence, termed Gamma-PFL. Specifically, we combine a loss function based on the gamma-divergence with fusion and sparse regularization terms to exploit similarities in regression coefficients across clients while enabling robust estimation of personalized models and variable selection. Furthermore, to efficiently solve the estimation problem in the federated server--client system, we develop an optimization algorithm that combines the Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers with the Majorization--Minimization algorithm. Numerical simulations showed that Gamma-PFL maintained relatively stable estimation accuracy as the contamination proportion or outlier magnitude increased, demonstrating its robustness to within-client data contamination. In addition, a real data analysis showed that Gamma-PFL achieved predictive performance comparable to or better than that of an existing personalized federated learning method.

papers.title: Raise or Check? Predicting the Necessity of Additional Fuzzing for Continuous Fuzzing
papers.abstract: Continuous fuzzing is used for vulnerability detection in Open Source Software (OSS). Large-scale services such as Google's OSS-Fuzz fuzz over 1,300 projects and have revealed more than 10,000 vulnerabilities. Despite this, a considerable time lag often exists between when a vulnerability is introduced and when it is detected (i.e., the window of exposure). Given the computational cost of additional fuzzing, we aim to allocate fuzzing resources efficiently using vulnerability-risk estimates. We propose RAISE (Risk-Aware Intensive Supplemental Execution Framework), a Just-In-Time (JIT) framework that prioritizes additional fuzzing for high-risk project-days. RAISE performs binary classification at the project-day granularity to estimate whether a vulnerability is introduced on a given day. We construct a dataset combining vulnerability-introducing commits from the OSV database with daily coverage and change metrics from OSS-Fuzz, covering 15 C/C++ projects and 15,210 project-days, of which 347 (2.28%) are vulnerability-introducing. In a cross-project validation setting, our best model, a Random Forest combining VCCFinder-based static features with dynamic fuzzing features, achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.74, substantially outperforming a random baseline; coverage metrics, led by PatchCoverage, are the most important features. In a simulation over 968 vulnerabilities comparing five allocation strategies, Simple-Regression was significantly more cost-efficient than the prediction-agnostic heuristics, spending 91.60 additional fuzzing sessions per detected vulnerability, roughly half the cost of the Median heuristic (171.89). RAISE shows that JIT vulnerability prediction with coverage-aware fuzzing features can effectively guide risk-aware allocation of continuous fuzzing resources.

papers.title: GARRET: Generative Feedback for Region Retrieval in Visual Documents
papers.abstract: Multimodal retrieval-augmented generation over visually rich documents requires evidence at a finer granularity than entire pages. Existing visual retrievers typically index or return full pages, whereas training region-level retrievers often requires costly query-to-region annotations or noisy model-generated labels. We introduce GARRET, a region-retrieval framework trained from (page, question, answer) triplets through differentiable generative feedback. A shared context-preserving retriever produces page and region multi-vector representations. During training, their retrieval scores define a soft routing distribution over candidate region crops. An auxiliary vision-language model attends to each crop separately, aggregates crop-specific contexts using the routing weights, and predicts the question followed by the answer under a next-token prediction objective. Gradients through the routing distribution assign query-conditioned credit to the indexed region representations, without requiring query-to-region annotations. At inference, the auxiliary model is removed. GARRET also reuses the contextualized region representations, together with page summary tokens, to construct a compact page representation. We introduce ViDoRe-V3-Region, a corpus-wide benchmark containing 200,682 fixed candidate regions across eight domains. GARRET achieves a macro nDCG@10 of 0.4126, outperforming the strongest visual baseline by 2.94 points. On page retrieval, it remains comparable to ColQwen2.5-v0.2 while indexing 47.8% fewer vectors per page.

papers.title: Primes in short intervals assuming the Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: In 2001 Baker, Harman, and Pintz proved, for $x$ sufficiently large, the existence of at least one prime in the sub-linear interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{40}}]$. But just how large is sufficiently large? In the current note I shall make the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem effective, but at an extremely high price. Contingent upon assuming validity of the Riemann hypothesis (RH), I shall show that the Baker--Harman--Pintz theorem holds for $x \geq 3.5\times 10^{90}$. Furthermore, again assuming RH, I shall also show that for any $0< m\leq15.831$ and $x \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[x,x+x^{\frac{1}{2} +\frac{1}{m}}]$, and that for $M\geq 2.29$ and $y \geq 1$ there is at least one prime in the interval $[y^M, (y+1)^M]$.

papers.title: The chemical evolution of the LMC from APOGEE abundances: a hybrid two-infall OMEGA+ analysis
papers.abstract: The Large Magellanic Cloud (LMC) provides resolved stellar abundances and star-formation histories that can be used together to test models of dwarf-galaxy chemical evolution. We investigated if the non-monotonic APOGEE $[\mathrm{Mg}/\mathrm{Fe}]$-$[\mathrm{Fe}/\mathrm{H}]$ sequence can be explained by a hybrid history that combines a second gas-infall episode with a temporary increase in star-formation efficiency (SFE). We selected 4933 LMC red-giant-branch stars from APOGEE-2 DR17. We fitted an adaptively binned median Mg sequence with the two-zone open-box code OMEGA+. The formal fitting objective contained only the Mg sequence. The metallicity distribution function (MDF), one-dimensional abundance distributions, star-formation history (SFH), present-day mass partition, SFR, and supernova (SN) rate were retained as posterior diagnostics. The best-fitting model reproduces the Mg sequence with an RMS residual of 0.01 dex and also gives a close posterior match to O. It contains two delayed-tau infall episodes, with the second beginning at $t_2=10.39$ Gyr and with integrated mass ratio $M_2/M_1=0.159$, followed by a temporary Gaussian SFE enhancement centred at $t=11.91$ Gyr. The second infall is represented by a mixture of enriched and primordial gas. The model reproduces the timing of the late SFH enhancement and yields a present SFR within the adopted comparison range. A hybrid second-infall and SFE-enhancement history is a plausible scenario for reproducing the observed LMC Mg median sequence. Our fit explains the LMC evolution fairly well, but the remaining small MDF, mass, and SN-rate discrepancies suggest that a selection-function-aware treatment of the stellar distributions is required for a stricter comparison.

papers.title: Wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations
papers.abstract: In this paper, we investigate wave breaking for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. We establish more general wave breaking criteria that strictly extend earlier wave breaking criteria for the nonlocal Whitham-type equations. The approach relies on analyzing the monotonicity and continuity properties of a linear combination comprising the supremum and infimum of the solution's slope. Further generalizations are demonstrated via applications to the Camassa-Holm equation, the $μ$-Camassa-Holm equation and the hyperelastic rod equation. Our refined approach yields more precise wave breaking criteria, thereby extending the theoretical understanding of singularity formation in dispersive waves.

papers.title: A 2/3-Approximation Algorithm for the Residual Maximum Matching Problem in General Graphs
papers.abstract: The residual maximum matching problem asks for a maximum matching whose deletion leaves a graph with the largest possible matching number. For unweighted graphs, previous work provides a $1/2$-approximation guarantee in general graphs and a $2/3$ guarantee in graphs with a perfect matching. We present a $2/3$-approximation algorithm running in $O(n^5)$ time, extending the latter guarantee to general graphs. The algorithm improves the residual matching number through single-edge exchanges involving free vertices. We prove that, for any maximum matching that admits no further improvement by such exchanges, the residual matching number is at least $2/3$ of the optimum, and we give an example showing that this bound is tight.

papers.title: Controlled-Z Gates via Floquet Coupling to Two Auxiliary States in Transmon Circuits
papers.abstract: High-fidelity entangling gates are essential for quantum information processing. In transmon circuits, higher excited states provide additional pathways for engineering interactions within the computational subspace. Here we demonstrate controlled-Z (CZ) gates that exploit two noncomputational states, $\ket{02}$ and $\ket{20}$, through selective Floquet coupling. The nontrivial parametric modulation can activate both auxiliary transitions from $\ket{11}$ while suppressing the leading exchange between $\ket{01}$ and $\ket{10}$. Based on this approach, we develop two gate protocols: a nonadiabatic round trip through a bright auxiliary superposition and adiabatic evolution along a zero-energy dark state, both achieving average gate fidelities above $99.99\%$ in numerical simulations. Control of the modulation phase further extends the bright-state protocol to conventional and unconventional geometric CZ gates. Effective-model simulations show that unconventional control improves tolerance to residual $ZZ$ coupling and static qubit-frequency offsets relative to conventional control over the parameter ranges examined. Simulations including neighboring spectator qubits show that the original nonadiabatic bright-state and adiabatic dark-state CZ protocols retain high gate fidelities. This framework offers new routes toward the experimental realization of CZ gates and their geometric implementations.

papers.title: From Generic to Dedicated: A Novel Optimizer for Online Continual Learning
papers.abstract: Online Continual Learning (OCL) requires models to learn from non-stationary data streams under a strict single-pass constraint, making them highly susceptible to catastrophic forgetting. While existing studies have explored various strategies from data, architecture, and optimization perspectives, the optimizer often directly uses generic approaches such as SGD and AdamW. In this work, we reveal a new link between optimization dynamics and OCL needs by recasting Polyak-Ruppert averaging as the engine of "plasticity" and Primal averaging as the anchor of "stability". This inspires our novel optimizer, SPIN (Stability-Plasticity INterpolation), which explicitly decouples plasticity and stability by interpolating between a fast-moving "plasticity" sequence and an adaptive "stability" sequence. We theoretically demonstrate that SPIN implicitly employs an inverse Hessian approximation, providing crucial Tikhonov regularization to damp noisy, single-sample Hessian estimates and mitigate forgetting. More importantly, SPIN can be seamlessly integrated into existing OCL methods by taking resulted gradients as input and replacing standard optimizers. Extensive experiments show that using SPIN instead of standard optimizers yields consistent and significant performance gains across multiple OCL approaches, including the challenging rehearsal-free setting and under strict memory constraints.

papers.title: Agentic discovery of interpretable car-following laws from multi-source trajectory data
papers.abstract: Car-following (CF) models is a fundamental component of microscopic traffic simulation and underpin the analysis of collective traffic dynamics, while its modeling becomes more challenging due to diverse human driving behaviors and the increasing presence of automated vehicle. Analytical CF models offer interpretable representations of longitudinal vehicle interactions, but their prescribed functional structures may limit the representation of heterogeneous driving behavior. This study proposes an agent-centered, physics-aware framework for the empirical discovery of CF laws from multi-source trajectory data. The framework iteratively combines agent-guided hypothesis generation, informed by traffic flow knowledge and state-dependent reconstruction errors, with evolutionary symbolic search and physics-aware multi-objective evaluation. Using NGSIM US-101, highD, and exiD, the framework discovers the Adaptive Equilibrium Response Model (AERM), which couples state-dependent relative-speed response with spacing-dependent equilibrium-speed restoration. AERM admits analytical equilibrium speed-spacing and flow-density relationships; its stability conditions are derived for the zero-delay formulation, and platoon simulations examine disturbance propagation. Evaluated against seven classical CF models on Shanghai naturalistic driving data, NGSIM I-80, and Waymo trajectories, AERM attains the lowest spacing and speed reconstruction errors under trajectory-specific calibration, reducing spacing RMSE by 9.11%, 7.59%, and 21.73% relative to the strongest baselines, and remains competitive under dataset-level shared parameters. These results demonstrate the fitting flexibility and analytical tractability of the discovered CF law, providing an interpretable basis for microscopic traffic simulation.

papers.title: A Novel Two-Level Domain Decomposition Method with Physically Motivated Coarse Space for Surface Acoustic Wave Device Simulations
papers.abstract: The surface acoustic wave (SAW) equations are fundamental in describing the operating principle of SAW devices, which are characterized by high operating frequency, multiphysics coupling, and defined on an unbounded domain. Finite element (FE) simulation is one of the most accurate numerical methods for such devices. However, the method usually leads to ill-conditioned linear systems with a large number of degrees of freedom (DOFs), limiting its application. To address this issue, based on the finite element tearing and interconnecting (FETI) algorithm, this paper proposes a domain decomposition method with iteration numbers stable with respect to number of subdomains, frequency and mesh size, named FETI-SAW. The main novelty is that the Dirichlet preconditioner combined with a Rayleigh-wave-based coarse space is constructed to produce a preconditioned iterative algorithm for the Lagrange multiplier linear system. In some sense, this method reflects the physical essence of the SAW equations. In numerical experiments, we take interdigital transducers (IDT) and SAW resonators as examples to demonstrate the efficiency of the FETI-SAW algorithm. Additionally, the MATLAB and C++ source codes accompanying this paper are provided.

papers.title: An Exact Polynomial-Time Algorithm for the Minimum Shared-Power Edge Cut Problem
papers.abstract: The Minimum Shared-Power Edge Cut (MSPEC) problem seeks to disconnect two designated terminals with minimum total power by assigning powers to graph vertices and deleting every edge for which the sum of the powers at its endpoints reaches its edge weight. Previous work gave a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme for this problem, while its exact computational complexity remained open. We prove that general MSPEC with nonnegative edge weights can be solved exactly in polynomial time. Specifically, we first use linear programming duality for each fixed cut to reformulate MSPEC as minimizing the maximum terminal-relaxed matching weight over all $s$-$t$ cuts. Then, we construct a terminal-copy extended graph that transforms the maximum-weight matching model with unconstrained terminal capacities for a fixed cut into an equivalent ordinary maximum-weight matching model. Next, we extend the submodularity of the unweighted maximum-matching cut function to nonnegative edge weights and prove that the restriction obtained by fixing the terminal copies on prescribed sides remains submodular. Consequently, MSPEC reduces to exact submodular function minimization. Once an optimal cut is obtained, a corresponding optimal power assignment can be recovered. This result resolves the open question concerning the exact computational complexity of general MSPEC.

papers.title: Extending Mechanisms
papers.abstract: Given an incentive-compatible mechanism for a single agent on a restricted domain of valuations, we consider its incentive-compatible extensions to the entire valuation space. We identify two extreme extensions: the "keep-the-menu" extension, which minimizes buyer payoffs and maximizes canonical prices pointwise, and the "keep-the-pricing" extension, which maximizes buyer payoffs and minimizes canonical prices pointwise.

papers.title: Influence of Ideal, Cubic, and Multiparameter Helmholtz Equations of State on the Static and Dynamic Performance of Porous Aerostatic Journal Bearings
papers.abstract: Porous aerostatic gas bearings are commonly modeled using the ideal-gas law, although non-ideal thermodynamic behavior may become relevant for alternative working fluids. This study quantifies the influence of the thermodynamic closure on the stationary and dynamic response of porous aerostatic journal bearings. A finite-volume formulation couples the compressible Reynolds equation with three-dimensional Darcy flow, retaining transient gas storage in both domains. Density is used as the primary thermodynamic variable, allowing the ideal-gas, van der Waals, Soave--Redlich--Kwong, Peng--Robinson, and multiparameter Helmholtz equations of state to be evaluated within an otherwise unchanged bearing model. Air, R1234yf, and R1234ze(E) are considered. For air, EOS-induced differences remain negligible over the investigated range. For the refrigerants, the ideal-gas approximation produces several-percent deviations, with supplied mass flow and dynamic force response being particularly sensitive. The cubic equations substantially reduce these deviations, with the employed Peng--Robinson formulation providing the closest agreement with the Helmholtz reference for both refrigerants at a computational cost comparable to the other cubic models. The results identify density and differential compressibility as the main thermodynamic quantities governing the propagation of EOS errors into mass transport and transient gas storage.

papers.title: SciDiagBench: A Type-Specific Benchmark for Human-Aligned Evaluation of Scientific Diagrams
papers.abstract: Recent agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in generating images from textual prompts, motivating their utilization for scientific diagram generation. Scientific diagrams naturally span diverse types, each characterized by distinct visual structures and content organization. Consequently, during peer review and other scientific evaluation, human experts naturally consider type-specific criteria when assessing their quality. However, existing VLM-based evaluation benchmarks fail to reflect the above human evaluation practices for two main reasons: 1) benchmark datasets typically lack a systematic categorization of different diagram types and thus adopt the same generic criteria for all diagrams, and 2) their evaluation criteria are often designed heuristically, without explicit alignment to human evaluation preferences. Motivated by these limitations, we introduce SciDiagBench, which consists of a benchmark dataset that systematically categorizes scientific diagrams into 11 types and a human preference-guided evaluation method. Specifically, SciDiagBench contains 165 scientific diagrams across 10 broad domains, with types including graphical abstracts, technical roadmaps, and illustrative cases. Based on this dataset, SciDiagBench develops an evaluation method that leverages a preference-guided calibration process to incorporate human preferences into the generation of type-specific criteria. Ultimately, SciDiagBench enables more reliable automated evaluation that better aligns with human evaluation across diverse scientific diagrams.

papers.title: Payoff Polarization and Garbage Concentration in a Stochastic Garbage Disposal Game
papers.abstract: We study a stochastic garbage disposal game on a finite graph in which agents transfer garbage through pairwise interactions governed by payoff-dependent Fermi probabilities. We investigate the long-term behavior of both payoffs and garbage distributions. We prove that payoff dispersion grows at least linearly in time almost surely, leading to payoff polarization, with the maximum and minimum payoffs diverging to positive and negative infinity, respectively. Moreover, the payoff range grows at least on the order of the square root of time. For garbage dynamics, we establish almost-sure concentration on a single agent in the two-agent case for any positive disposal efficiency. When disposal is complete and the underlying graph is connected, we further prove that all garbage becomes concentrated on a single agent after a finite random time, although the agent holding the garbage may change over time. These results characterize the emergence of payoff inequality and garbage concentration in stochastic competitive interactions on networks.

papers.title: Flavor decomposition of electromagnetic multipole moments in $[q_1q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquarks: Light-quark analogs of $T_{cs1}(2900)^0$ with $J^P = 1^+$
papers.abstract: We present a systematic study of the magnetic dipole and electric quadrupole moments of compact $[q_1 q_2][\bar q_3 \bar c]$ tetraquark states with quantum numbers $J^P = 1^+$, in the diquark--antidiquark picture and within the light-cone QCD sum rule framework. By performing a flavor decomposition across all admissible $u/d$ configurations, we show that the charm-quark contribution to the electromagnetic moments vanishes algebraically at the operator level -- a structural feature of the specific spin organization adopted here, in which the heavy antiquark resides in a pseudoscalar antidiquark, distinct from the dynamical $1/m_c$ suppression operative in alternative compact constructions and in hadronic molecules. The magnetic moments follow a coherent light-flavor pattern -- positive for $uu$-, negative for $dd$-, and suppressed for mixed-flavor diquarks -- and the quadrupole moments are non-zero throughout, corresponding, in the customary geometrical interpretation, to intrinsically deformed charge distributions. We further identify the dimensionless multipole ratio $\mathcal{D}/μ$ as a structural observable, independent of the normalization of the interpolating current, which probes the relative geometry of the spin-current and charge distributions complementary to the absolute moments. Taken together, the algebraic decoupling of the charm contribution and the operator-level distinction it implies among different singly-heavy tetraquark architectures constitute methodological signatures that discriminate among the corresponding internal organizations and, to the extent that a physical candidate is dominated by one of them, among compact and molecular interpretations.

papers.title: Beta-expansions induced by general Parry polynomials and sharp iteration asymptotics of their transfer operators
papers.abstract: This paper generalizes previous results to any Parry polynomials $p_n(z)$ \cite{Pa} of finite degree $n\geq 2$. Let $β>1$ be the unique positive root of $p_n$ and consider the transfer operator $\mathscr{P}$ induced by the map $[0,1]\ni x\mapsto βx-\lfloor βx\rfloor \in [0,1)$. Suppose all other roots of $p_n$ have magnitude less than one. Then for any smooth function $F$ on $[0,1]$ we prove two term asymptotics in $L^\infty$ of the form \begin{equation*} \big(\mathscr{P}^r(F)\big)(\cdot)= u(\cdot) \int_0^1 F(x)\: \mathrm{d} x +β^{-r}v(\cdot) \big (F(1)-F(0)\big )+o(β^{-r}),\quad r\geq 1, \end{equation*} where $u$ is piecewise constant and $\mathscr{P}u=u$, while $v$ is piecewise equal to a polynomial of degree one and $\mathscr{P}v= β^{-1}v$. When $\mathscr{P}$ is restricted to functions of bounded variation $BV([0,1])$, it is known that $\vert z \vert\leq β^{-1}$ contains its essential spectrum. Thus the contribution coming from $v$ in the above estimate is not guaranteed if $F$ is not smooth enough. Furthermore, we show that when $\mathscr{P}$ is restricted to $BV([0,1])$ then any $\vert z \vert<β^{-1}$ is an eigenvalue with infinite multiplicity. Moreover, we construct a meromorphic extension of $(\mathscr{P}-z)^{-1}$ to the domain $\vert z \vert>β^{-1}$, where the finite rank poles are numbers $ζ$ with $β^{-1}<\vert ζ\vert\leq 1$ such that $βζ$ is a root of $p_n(z)$.
